subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 41-year-old man who works at a wool and hide processing plant develops 3 days of fever, myalgias, nonproductive cough, and chest discomfort. Chest radiograph shows a widened mediastinum with pleural effusions. Blood cultures grow large gram-positive rods that form spores, and the colonies have a halo of projections resembling a medusa head.
question: Which of the following components of the responsible toxin acts as an adenylyl cyclase?
explanation_correct: Anthrax toxin has three exotoxin components: protective antigen, lethal factor, and edema factor. Edema factor acts as an adenylyl cyclase, raising intracellular cAMP and upsetting homeostasis to produce edema and necrosis. Protective antigen is the binding component, while lethal factor inhibits MAP kinase and promotes macrophage apoptosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: The poly d-glutamate polypeptide capsule is a separate antiphagocytic virulence factor of Bacillus anthracis and is not part of the toxin complex.
explanation_incorrect.B: Lecithinase is a phospholipase that causes myonecrosis and hemolysis in Clostridium perfringens infection, not a component of anthrax toxin.
explanation_incorrect.D: Protective antigen is the cell-binding component that delivers the other two factors into the cytosol; it has no adenylyl cyclase activity, though antibodies against it are protective, hence the name.
explanation_incorrect.E: Lethal factor is a protease that inhibits MAP kinase and drives macrophage apoptosis, producing necrosis and shock rather than a cAMP increase.

educationalObjective: Anthrax toxin comprises protective antigen, lethal factor (MAP kinase inhibition and macrophage apoptosis), and edema factor (adenylyl cyclase raising cAMP).

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 37-year-old goat farmer in a rural area notices an enlarging painless lesion on his forearm. Over several days it becomes a painless papule surrounded by vesicles, then ulcerates with a black necrotic eschar and surrounding nonpitting edema. He is afebrile and feels otherwise well. Gram stain of the exudate shows large gram-positive rods with central spores.
question: Which of the following best describes this presentation?

options.text: Cutaneous anthrax, which uncommonly progresses to bacteremia and death
Cutaneous diphtheria with a gray pseudomembrane

explanation_correct: Cutaneous anthrax begins as a painless papule surrounded by vesicles, which becomes an ulcer with a black painless necrotic eschar and local edema, typically after contact with contaminated animals or animal products. It uncommonly progresses to bacteremia and death, in contrast to pulmonary anthrax, which is often fatal. Both forms may be complicated by hemorrhagic meningitis.

explanation_incorrect.B: Streptococcal necrotizing fasciitis produces severe pain out of proportion to findings with dusky bullous skin and systemic toxicity, quite unlike this painless localized lesion in a well patient.
explanation_incorrect.C: Gas gangrene from C perfringens presents with soft tissue crepitus, myonecrosis, and rapid systemic deterioration after contaminated wound injury.
explanation_incorrect.D: Cutaneous or wound diphtheria produces a grayish membrane over a mucosal or skin defect and is caused by club-shaped rods with metachromatic granules, not by spore-forming rods.
explanation_incorrect.E: Ecthyma gangrenosum is a rapidly progressive necrotic cutaneous lesion caused by Pseudomonas bacteremia in immunocompromised patients, and its lesion is painful with surrounding erythema rather than a painless eschar.

educationalObjective: Cutaneous anthrax is a painless papule that ulcerates into a black eschar and rarely disseminates, whereas pulmonary anthrax is far more lethal.

subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 30-year-old laboratory technician is exposed to a suspicious white powder during an incident involving a suspected bioterrorist release at a postal facility. She has no symptoms yet and is wearing standard protective equipment when she presents to the occupational health clinic within 6 hours of exposure.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate management for this asymptomatic exposed individual?

options.text: Oral rehydration solution and supportive care

explanation_correct: Prophylaxis against anthrax after exposure to aerosolized spores is ciprofloxacin or doxycycline. Pulmonary anthrax follows inhalation of spores, most commonly from contaminated animals or animal products but also a potential bioweapon, and presents with flulike symptoms that rapidly progress to fever, pulmonary hemorrhage, mediastinitis with a widened mediastinum, and shock.

explanation_incorrect.A: Oral rehydration is the cornerstone of cholera management and would do nothing to prevent inhalational anthrax.
explanation_incorrect.B: Diphtheria antitoxin with erythromycin treats Corynebacterium diphtheriae exotoxin disease and has no activity against anthrax.
explanation_incorrect.C: Intrapartum penicillin prophylaxis is the group B streptococcal prevention strategy, which is unrelated to spore exposure.
explanation_incorrect.E: Rifampin, ciprofloxacin, or ceftriaxone prophylaxis is the postexposure approach for close contacts of meningococcal or Haemophilus influenzae type b disease, not anthrax.

educationalObjective: Postexposure anthrax prophylaxis is ciprofloxacin or doxycycline, and pulmonary anthrax shows a widened mediastinum and rapid progression to shock.
